description: FedEx, founded in 1971, is a multinational delivery services company known for its overnight shipping and pioneering tracking systems. Headquartered in Memphis, FedEx operates in more than 220 countries and territories, providing an array of services including express transportation, freight, e-commerce, and business solutions.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription:
The parcel delivery giant reported revenue of $93.5 billion (up 11.4%) and profits of $3.8 billion (down 26.9%). Rajesh Subramaniam succeeded founder Frederick Smith as CEO on June 1, 2022.

  • In February 2023, FedEx cut 10% of global officer and director jobs, a cost-cutting move prompted in part by diminishing revenue from e-commerce.

  • Subramaniam announced in April 2023 that FedEx would combine its express and ground businesses. Smith had long defended keeping the units separate, even as analysts and investors urged their merger to simplify operations. Subramaniam says the move will help consumers understand pricing and shipping options more easily.

  • FedEx is the fourth largest employer on the Fortune 500.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: As one of the largest delivery services companies in the U.S., FedEx has employed thousands of workers on the front lines of the pandemic. To support them, the company debuted a new health care advocate program called Choose Well Care Connect, which provides those workers with a single point of contact whenever they have a health care need, helping them navigate a complex system of vendors. It’s also made 24/7 confidential counseling available to all employees, eligible dependents, and household members, even if they aren’t actively participating in the plan. The company facilitates career advancement through the FedEx Learning Center, which offers over 25,000 online courses; Aspire, which provides hourly employees access to experiential learning, coaching, and development opportunities; and direct tuition assistance for higher education. “I greatly appreciate the mentoring and guidance the managers at FedEx offer to everyone,” says one staffer. “I feel there is a sense of caring from management to their employees.”

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: The delivery services giant climbed six spots to No. 39 on this year’s Fortune 500. Thanks to an increase in e-commerce during the pandemic; the company predicts its deliveries could exceed 100 million a day in calendar 2022. FedEx will experience an epochal change in leadership on June 1, 2022, when founder and CEO Frederick W. Smith will step down after more than 50 years at the helm. Raj Subramaniam will succeed Smith, who remained the largest shareholder in FedEx as of March 2022, with a stake of about 7.3%.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Second only to United Parcel Service in the U.S. package-shipping business, FedEx said COVID-19 affected “virtually all revenue and expense line items” during the final quarter of its latest fiscal year, which ended May 31, 2020, dinging revenues 0.7% to $69.2 billion versus the year prior. Despite the disruption, profits surged an eye-popping 138% to $1.29 billion, nearly rivaling much bigger UPS’s $1.34 billion in profits. The jump is mostly due to earlier costly investments FedEx made to revamp its historically business-centric delivery network so it can better cater to residential customers.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Second only to United Parcel Service in the package-shipping business, FedEx grew faster than its rival in 2019. The delivery dynamo brought in nearly $69.7 billion in its most recent fiscal year, up 6.5% from FY 2018. Still, FedEx investors despaired over a once marquee customer, Amazon, turning to a competitor. Readying itself for the fight of its life, FedEx spent big sums to revamp its delivery network, known primarily for catering to businesses, to go the “last mile” and drop off boxes on residential doorsteps. Costly investments, in part, caused profits to plummet more than 88%, to $540 million. On a December earnings call, FedEx’s chief financial officer described the hit as “horrific.” But instead of slashing costs, FedEx has swelled its ranks, adding nearly 30,000 more employees over the past year.
